items.title: Can Mondelez Sustain Growth Momentum Across Gum and Candy?
items.summary: Mondelez's gum and candy growth is fueled by volume, pricing, wider distribution and innovation, though its momentum beyond the first half remains unclear.

items.title: Mondelēz brings Biscoff partnership to US with Toblerone truffles
items.summary: The launch comes as the snacking giant’s collaboration with the cookie brand in other countries “surpassed even our expectations,” an executive said.

items.title: Pepsi’s Fall Continues: One Prominent Firm’s Resolute Target Implies 41% Gains Moving Forward
items.summary: PepsiCo has shed nearly 7% this year while the S&P 500 climbed double digits, yet one prominent firm refuses to abandon a price target that towers far above Wall Street consensus and hinges on a very specific set of dominoes falling into place.

items.title: Should You Buy PepsiCo Stock Because Its International Business Keeps Accelerating?
items.summary: PepsiCo (PEP) stock traded at $129.75 on September 18, the lowest price of its past 52 weeks. The worry is North America, where sales of snacks and drinks have disappointed. Yet the part of PepsiCo that sells outside the U.S. is growing faster and earning more on each sale. The share price appears to give that part little credit.

items.title: Mondelēz names new chief procurement officer as cocoa market stabilizes
items.summary: Formerly SVP of cocoa enterprise, Zakaria Dahkoun took over the role in August as the company sees better supply security for the key ingredient.

items.title: 2 Nasdaq 100 Stocks for Long-Term Investors and 1 We Turn Down
items.summary: The Nasdaq 100 (^NDX) is home to some of the biggest success stories in tech and growth investing. However, certain stocks in the index face challenges like profitability concerns, rising costs, or shifts in market trends.

items.title: 2 S&P 500 Stocks Worth Your Attention and 1 We Question
items.summary: While the S&P 500 (^GSPC) includes industry leaders, not every stock in the index is a winner. Some companies are past their prime, weighed down by poor execution, weak financials, or structural headwinds.
